title: 3D positioning of tagged DNA loci by widefield and super-resolution fluorescence imaging of fixed yeast nuclei
protocol: Grow cells overnight at 25°C while shaking (180–220 RPM) in a 50 mL aerated and sterile conical tube containing 3–8 mL of liquid medium (SC or YAP supplemented with the desired carbon source).
Dilute the culture to 1–2.10^6 cells/mL with fresh medium if cell concentration exceeds specified limits.
Let cells grow for at least 4 hours before starting the experiment after dilution.
Add 3 times 2,7 μg of alpha-factor per mL to a culture at 5.10^6 cells/mL at 25°C for G1 synchronization.
Divide the synchronized cell culture and add 100mM of hydroxyurea (HU) to half of the initial culture for pre-treatment with HU for 15 minutes before release.
Keep the other half untreated to release cells from alpha-factor without genotoxic agents.
Wash out alpha-factor by filtration.
Transfer cells into fresh medium for 30 minutes for untreated culture in S phase condition.
Transfer cells into medium supplemented with genotoxic drugs such as 0.2M hydroxyurea and 0.033% methylmethane sulfonate for 60 minutes for HU pretreated culture in damaged condition.
Add hydroxyurea to the culture medium at the end of G1 synchronization, at least 15 minutes prior to alpha-factor removal.
Add methyl methanesulfonate solution immediately after washing out alpha-factor.
Alternatively, treat unsynchronized exponentially growing cells directly with genotoxic drugs for 1 or 2 hours.
Grow cells overnight in repressive 2% glucose medium for random positioning of the GAL1-GAL10 locus.
Grow cells overnight in non-repressive raffinose medium for preferential nuclear periphery localization of the GAL1-GAL10 locus.
Induce galactose expression by transferring cells from raffinose to galactose at a cell concentration of 3.106 cells/mL.
Incubate cells for 90 minutes in galactose after transfer from raffinose medium.
Grow MATa cells overnight in 2% glucose medium.
Treat cells three times with alpha-factor every hour at a concentration of 2,7 μg/ml culture at 5.106 cells/mL and 25°C.
Incubate cells for 2.5 hours after the last treatment with alpha-factor.
Collect 1.5 ml of yeast culture at the time of interest.
Spin collected yeast culture for 1 min at 10,000 × g.
Remove supernatant from spun yeast culture.
Resuspend cell pellet in 50 μl of 4% freshly prepared PFA.
Fix cells with PFA for 30-60 seconds.
Spin fixed cells immediately at 10,000 × g for 30 s.
Remove supernatant and wash with 500 μL of PBS.
Repeat washes twice.
Resuspend cell pellets in 100 to 300 μl of PBS.
Pipette 40 μl of fixed cells on a concanavalin A-coated coverslip.
Incubate for 15–20 min at 20°C–25°C.
Remove excess yeast suspension by washing with 50 μL of PBS and removing the liquid.
Repeat wash step twice.
Add a few drops of mounting medium to remove excess liquid.
Stick a SecureSeal adhesive imaging spacer on glass slides.
Peel the clear plastic from the adhesive imaging spacer.
Stick the yeast-covered coverslip on the adhesive imaging spacer.
Remove excess mounting medium with a precision wipe.
Cells are ready for imaging.
